| 2026-07-11 | B4-roles-1 — GUC staff bypass → DB-role staff bypass (owner decision: separate DB roles, taskdb `#662`)           | Owner-confirmed hardening: every patient-wall policy's staff bypass was `NULLIF(current_setting('app.actor', true), '') = 'staff'` — a plain session GUC settable by ANY session, including a patient session (provably spoofable by injection, not a real security boundary). Replaced it with a role-membership check via a new canonical helper `app.is_staff()` (schema `app`, `SECURITY INVOKER`, `STABLE`, `SET search_path = pg_catalog`): `SELECT pg_has_role(current_user, 'app_staff', 'MEMBER')` — `app_staff` is a single, fixed, canonical role name spelled out ONLY inside this function (not duplicated in any predicate). `rls-sql-renderer.mjs`'s `renderStaffActorCheck()` is the ONE chokepoint every staff-or-patient wrapper (`renderStaffOrPatientPredicate`, `..PatientChainPredicate`, `..ConditionalPatientPredicate`, `..ConditionalChainPatientPredicate`, `..PolymorphicPatientPredicate`, plus `p0-9-enforce-descriptors.mjs`'s fk_path enforce branch) calls through, so changing that one function flipped ALL 5 patient-ownership predicate shapes at once — verified by re-running `check-p0-8-{3,4,5}-policy-generator.mjs`/`check-p0-8-sql-renderer.mjs`/`check-p0-9-enforce-descriptors.mjs` (updated their hardcoded `app.actor`-substring assertions to `app.is_staff()`). Registered in `meta/_journal.json` (idx 175). Added `deploy/postgres/p0-5b-role-split-staff-patient.sql` (extends B5/P0.5 — separate file, not touching the existing parameterized `p0-5-role-split.sql`): creates the two FIXED roles `app_staff`/`app_patient` (both `LOGIN NOBYPASSRLS`, no password/credential provisioned — dormant), asserts (fatal `SELECT 1/0` under `ON_ERROR_STOP`) both roles are LOGIN/non-superuser/non-createrole/NOBYPASSRLS, and — the actual security invariant — asserts `app_patient` has NO membership in `app_staff` (`REVOKE app_staff FROM app_patient` run unconditionally/defensively first, idempotent). No table grants (deliberately deferred to B5-v2, a separate task). Reversible (`-v p0_5b_down=1`), verified live. Added `docs/_TODO/SAAS_FOUNDATION/scripts/smoke-b4-roles-1-staff-role-boundary.mjs` (new, complements — does not replace — `smoke-r2-real-policy-isolation.mjs`) proving live on a scratch DB, reading the REAL committed `p0-5b-role-split-staff-patient.sql` + migration-0175 preamble (not re-typed copies): (a) a session authorized as `app_staff` → `app.is_staff()=true` → sees BOTH patients' rows org-wide, on two REAL rendered policies (direct-column AND a chain/EXISTS shape, via the actual renderer functions); (b) a session authorized as `app_patient` (not a member of `app_staff`) → `app.is_staff()=false` → with `app.patient_user_id` set, sees ONLY its own row, never the other patient's, on both shapes; (c) **the money proof** — still as `app_patient`, `SET ROLE app_staff` is REJECTED by Postgres itself (`permission denied to set role`) — proven via a real non-superuser `session_user` (established by `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION app_patient`, which — unlike `SET ROLE` — changes `session_user` itself, so the subsequent `SET ROLE`'s permission check is genuinely against `app_patient`'s own memberships, not the harness's `postgres` superuser bootstrap); (d) empty context (no `app.org`/`app.patient_user_id`, still `app_patient`) denies both shapes, fail-closed. **Documented Postgres finding (not fudged, not asserted as a bug):** `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION app_staff` attempted from the SAME already-`app_patient`-authorized session unexpectedly SUCCEEDS in this superuser-bootstrapped harness — Postgres's `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION` permission check is against the connection's ORIGINALLY AUTHENTICATED role (fixed for the connection's life, here `postgres`, a real superuser — by design, so `RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION` can always restore it), not the current `session_user`; a real production connection authenticated directly AS `app_patient` (not descended from a superuser) would not have this escape hatch. Proof (c) via `SET ROLE` is therefore the valid, harness-independent test and is the one this smoke asserts on. Fixed by replacing the raw query with `SELECT (NOT pg_has_role('app_patient', 'app_staff', 'MEMBER'))::int` — same predicate `app.is_staff()` itself evaluates, so the assertion can no longer diverge from the real check. **(2, MED) migration `0175` silently preserved a pre-existing object's OWNER:** `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS app` / `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION app.is_staff()` are both no-ops/replace-in-place on an existing object and neither re-asserts ownership — if a lower-trust role had squatted `app`/`app.is_staff()` (name-squatting ahead of the legitimate migration) and the migration later ran with enough privilege to bypass ownership checks (e.g. as a superuser, a real deploy/bootstrap pattern), it would replace the function BODY while leaving OWNERSHIP with the squatter, who could then silently rewrite `app.is_staff()` back to `SELECT true` at will. Fixed by adding `ALTER SCHEMA app OWNER TO CURRENT_USER` right after `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS app`, `ALTER FUNCTION app.is_staff() OWNER TO CURRENT_USER` right after the `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`, and an explicit `REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA app FROM PUBLIC` (belt-and-suspenders, CREATE SCHEMA already grants nothing to PUBLIC by default) — all 3 are harmless no-ops on every clean/idempotent run where this migration's own role already owns both objects; they only change behavior in the squatting-attack case, where they either reclaim ownership (privileged migrator) or the migration was already failing loudly beforehand (non-privileged migrator: Postgres's own "must be owner" check on `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`/`GRANT` already blocks a non-owner, non-superuser migrator — confirmed live, see Checks). | 2026-07-10 | T0.4 S3 audit refix (taskdb #647)                                                                                 | Independent audit of commit `71b05b493` (row above) confirmed 2 defects and rejected the commit; this pass fixes exactly those 2, nothing else. **Defect 1 (HIGH, `mergeIntegratorUsers.ts`):** the merge M2M route (`userMergeM2mRoute.ts`) never wrapped `mergeIntegratorUsers` in an organization principal, so `getCurrentOrganizationPrincipalId()` was always `undefined` at runtime; combined with a winner having 0 or >1 active orgs, `organizationIdForIntegratorUserSql`'s 2-branch `COALESCE(principal, winnerSingleActiveOrg)` resolved to SQL `NULL`, so all 8 reparent UPDATEs (`message_drafts`, `conversations`, `user_questions`, `contacts`, `user_reminder_rules`, `content_access_grants`, `user_subscriptions`, `mailing_logs`) would zero out a previously-valid `organization_id` — an isolation regression. Fixed both ends: (a) `organizationIdForIntegratorUserSql` now takes an `existingOrganizationIdColumn` param and adds it as a 3rd `COALESCE` branch (e.g. `contacts.organization_id`) — Postgres resolves a bare table reference in an UPDATE's SET list to the pre-update row value, so the SET clause can now only ever preserve-or-improve `organization_id`, never null it out; all 8 call sites updated with their own table's column. (b) `userMergeM2mRoute.ts`'s `/api/integrator/users/merge` handler now resolves the winner's org via the same per-user→deployment-fallback path as webhooks/request-contact (`resolveOrganizationIdForIntegratorUserId` then `resolveDeploymentOrganizationId`, both newly threaded through `BersoncareUserMergeM2mDeps` and wired in `routes.ts` from the existing `createResolveOrganizationIdForIntegratorUserId`/`createResolveDeploymentOrganizationId` factories) and runs the merge under `runWithOrganizationPrincipal` when resolvable. **Defect 2 (MED, `channelUsers.ts`):** `resolveDeploymentSingleActiveOrganizationId`'s `SELECT id FROM public.be_organizations ORDER BY id LIMIT 2` ignored `is_active`, so 1 active + 1 deactivated org would return 2 rows → resolve to `null` → silently disable the channel-binding fallback. Added `WHERE is_active = true`. Implemented, guards ADDED on top of (not replacing) the existing three: (1) new `assertTestDatabaseOrDie(db)` — hardcoded `ALLOWED_TEST_DB_NAME = "bersoncarebot_test"` (canonical name per `docs/ARCHITECTURE/SERVER CONVENTIONS.md`, "Тест-БД `bersoncarebot_test` на том же PG16"), strict `===` equality (empty string, unknown name, or any name that merely contains the substring are all refused identically), runs before any config read/connection/write, no override flag by design (owner's ruling is TEST-only, full stop — an escape hatch would be a backdoor around it). (3) `git rm --cached` the file + new `.gitignore` entry (with an inline comment naming why: rewrites real credentials, TEST-only, don't re-add) so it stays on disk, untracked.
